topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Hallmarks and Progression
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the learning outcomes, historical framework, and foundational concepts of tumor progression across the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Sustained Proliferative Signaling and Evasion of Growth Suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular receptors and downstream signaling cascades drive continuous cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Blockade of Terminal Differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how oncogenic changes arrest cell maturation and maintain proliferative states in both hematological malignancies and epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the molecular mechanisms by which cancer cells disrupt the p53 pathway and the mitochondrial apoptotic machinery to evade programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence Bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer cells overcome the Hayflick limit and stress-induced arrest through telomere maintenance and reactivation of telomerase.

topics.label: Reprogramming Energy Metabolism and Oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the switch to aerobic glycolysis and the epigenetic consequences of metabolic enzyme mutations during tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Induction of Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how tumors trigger new blood vessel formation to overcome hypoxia and sustain tissue growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Inefficiencies of Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the steps, selective pressures, diagnostic markers, and genomic features associated with cancer dissemination to secondary sites.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Closing Remarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer summarizes the overlapping nature of the hallmarks, references recent literature, and concludes the session.
